how_to_run: From this folder: `python3 ../../framework-evals/run_eval.py <out-dir> [<eval-id>...] --evals evals.json [--tier core|regression|all] [--runs N] [--parallel N] [--dry-run] [--yes]`. Each eval is tagged `tier`: core (deconstruct 18's (core) items and rules 14's core list: routing, the wrong place, the light path's switch, safety and fail-closed, cold entry with work that already runs, and the first-time-leader journey on each platform) gates the release and runs three times; regression is everything else, run before each cohort release. The runner builds each fixture (`dir:` folders, mostly `../../framework-fixtures/`, or a name from fixtures/make_fixture.py), runs the skill isolated (harness.py), plays the leader from students/ on a simulated platform (`platform`, `platform_faults`), and grades: check_scripted.py for scripted expectations (quote checks against approved-lines.json, never the skill), grade_eval.py and the judge rubric for judged ones. Without --yes it prints the cost estimate and stops. Validate edits with `python3 ../../framework-evals/validate_evals.py evals.json --build-fixtures --strict-tiers` and `python3 ../../framework-evals/check_quotes.py evals evals.json`. Effort is counted in leader actions (`action_target`), never time. A core eval marked `core_runs: 1` (one that runs only on Microsoft 365 or Codex) runs once in the core round, and its one valid run counts (run_eval.py --help).
